name: UDR, Inc.
executive_summary: UDR, Inc. is a large-cap US multifamily REIT owning 165 stabilised communities (55,240 homes at year-end 2025) across 21 markets, with a portfolio tilt toward coastal and sunbelt metros. The quantitative screen rates the name a buy on cash generation, dividend yield, GARP-style valuation, and balance-sheet quality (7/22 models passed; composite 62%). The investment case rests on a 4.4% dividend yield, ~6.9% FCF yield, and low-single-digit same-store NOI growth, supported by active asset recycling and share repurchases. The central debate is whether modest organic growth and multifamily supply headwinds are adequately compensated by cash returns, or whether reported earnings inflation from dispositions masks underlying momentum. Deep research broadly confirms the screen’s income-and-quality angle, but flags earnings volatility and geographic concentration as reasons for measured rather than aggressive sizing.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, UDR offers a cash-return-oriented entry into a defensive sector. Shelter demand remains structurally supported—filings cite mortgage-rate-driven homeownership affordability as a tailwind—and UDR’s same-store revenue and NOI grew 2.4% and 2.3% respectively in FY2025 (10-K, filed 17 February 2026), with FY2024 at 2.3%/1.5%. That is not high growth, but it is steady and cash-backed.

The screen’s buy signal aligns with observable business quality:

- **Cash and dividends:** The screen passes FCF Yield, High Dividend Yield, and Dividend Growth. FY2025 declared distributions were $1.72 per share (+1.2% YoY; 10-K). Q1 2026 declared a $0.435 quarterly dividend ($1.74 annualised; 10-Q, filed 30 April 2026).
- **Valuation/GARP:** Lynch PEG and Neff PEGY pass with screen PEG 0.18 and P/E 26.9—typical for REITs where GAAP earnings are depreciation-heavy and FCF is the better anchor.
- **Quality/risk:** Piotroski F-Score and Earnings Quality passes sit alongside investment-grade balance-sheet management: total debt fell to $5.66bn at 31 March 2026 from $5.82bn at year-end 2025, and the company confirmed covenant compliance (Q1 2026 10-Q).
- **Capital discipline:** FY2025 repurchases of 3.3m shares (~$117.8m; 10-K) and Q1 2026 repurchases of 2.8m shares (~$100m; 10-Q) support per-share value. Asset sales and JV recycling generated substantial proceeds in 2025 and Q1 2026.

UDR is not a deep cyclical value trap; it is a quality income compounder trading at a screen-implied discount to its cash-return profile, with the caveat that headline P/E is distorted by non-recurring gains.
financial_review:
*Primary source: SEC EDGAR filing bodies. Absolute revenue/FCF totals from filing highlights and consolidated statements where available; Yahoo fallback noted where annual statement tables are truncated in the extract.*

**Annual results (10-K)**

| Metric | FY2025 (10-K, 17 Feb 2026) | FY2024 (10-K, 18 Feb 2025) |
|---|---|---|
| Total revenue growth | +2.4% | +2.7% |
| Same-store revenue growth | +2.4% | +2.3% |
| Same-store NOI growth | +2.3% | +1.5% |
| Net income attributable to common | $372.9m | $84.8m |
| Annual dividend (declared) | $1.72 | $1.70 |
| Real estate at cost | $16.49bn | $16.21bn |
| Share repurchases | 3.3m shares / ~$117.8m | Not highlighted |

FY2025 net income rose sharply, but filings attribute this primarily to higher disposition gains (including JV contributions), higher NOI, the absence of a $37.3m loan reserve recorded in 2024, and lower depreciation—not a step-change in core operations. Same-store fundamentals improved modestly but consistently.

*Fallback (Yahoo `financials_annual.json`, used because 10-K body extracts lack full income-statement tables):* FY2025 total revenue $1,712m, operating cash flow $903m, free cash flow $614m, total debt $6.0bn, net debt $5.8bn, diluted EPS $1.13.

**Interim results (10-Q)**

| Period | Rental income | Net income to common | Notable items |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2026 (10-Q, 30 Apr 2026) | $423.3m (+0.8% YoY) | $188.6m | Gain on sale $157.4m; OCF $128.7m (vs $156.2m prior year) |
| Q1 2025 (10-Q, 1 May 2025) | $419.8m | $75.5m | Gain on sale $47.9m |
| Q2 2025 (10-Q, 31 Jul 2025) | $423.0m (+2.3% YoY) | $36.5m | — |
| Q3 2025 (10-Q, 30 Oct 2025) | $429.3m (+2.7% YoY) | $39.2m | — |

Interim rental income shows steady low-single-digit YoY growth through 2025 into Q1 2026. Q1 2026 reported earnings are not representative of run-rate operations: a $362m gross disposition (four communities, 1,159 homes) drove most of the quarter’s profit. Operating cash flow declined YoY in Q1 2026, which warrants monitoring.

**Balance sheet and liquidity (Q1 2026 10-Q)**

- Total assets: $10.33bn; total debt (net): $5.66bn; weighted average interest rate 3.37%.
- ~89% of real estate (by gross book value) is unencumbered; secured debt is 11%.
- Debt maturities in 2026: ~$525m (including commercial paper).
- Revolving credit facility: $1.3bn capacity; $135m drawn at quarter-end.
- Commercial paper: $170m outstanding (down from $445m at year-end 2025).
- Covenant compliance confirmed at 31 March 2026.

**Gaps:** Q2 2026 results are not yet in the filing index (earnings release was scheduled for 27 July 2026 per news). Eight recent 8-K filings (Jan–May 2026) have no body extracts. Full-year FFO/AFFO reconciliation tables are not present in the truncated 10-K bodies; treat GAAP net income as an unreliable earnings proxy.
risks_and_flags:
**Geographic concentration.** FY2025 10-K discloses ~74.5% of NOI from eight markets (Metro D.C., Boston, Orange County, San Francisco Bay Area, Dallas, New York, Seattle, Tampa). A downturn in any one region would disproportionately affect results.

**Multifamily supply and rent regulation.** Filing risk factors highlight new-supply competition, rent control/stabilisation, and eviction regulation as material threats to occupancy and rent growth. Revenue growth guidance in the 10-K explicitly warns that 2026 same-store performance could be pressured by supply, concessions, and bad debt.

**Interest-rate and refinancing risk.** Despite a largely fixed-rate profile (hedged term loan at 4.04% on $175m until October 2027), variable-rate commercial paper, revolver, and ~$525m of 2026 maturities create rollover exposure in a ~4.7% 10-year Treasury environment (macro context, colour only).

**Earnings quality / non-recurring items.** FY2025 and Q1 2026 net income is heavily influenced by disposition and JV gains ($47.9m–$195m range cited in 10-K activity). Screen “growth=151.6%” likely reflects this distortion; core rental growth is ~2–3%.

**Credit exposure in capital programme.** A $37.3m loan reserve on a mezzanine facility was recorded in 2024 (FY2025 10-K). Notes receivable totalled $154m at Q1 2026 with a $0.6m allowance—small but a reminder of development/JV counterparty risk.

**Governance / going concern.** No going-concern language identified. Item 3 (Defaults Upon Senior Securities) is marked N/A across filings reviewed. No pension obligations flagged (typical for US REITs).

**Operational.** Q1 2026 operating cash flow fell 18% YoY despite higher rental income, partly reflecting working-capital movements; sustained weakness would challenge dividend coverage from operations alone (though REITs also fund distributions via FFO add-backs and asset sales).

No material M&A, management change, or regulatory enforcement actions were identified in the manifest. News is tilted toward earnings previews and analyst ratings rather than operational breakthroughs—useful for sentiment, not for replacing filing-based fundamentals.
research_rationale: Deep research confirms the screen’s cash-yield and quality thesis—steady same-store growth, dividend growth, active buybacks, and covenant-compliant deleveraging—but headline earnings are gain-distorted and geographic/supply risks cap conviction at accumulate rather than strong buy.
